newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ALPINE SKIING-GHEDINA LEADS TRAINING RUN.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-GHEDINA LEADS TRAINING RUN.

text.p: Italy's Kristian Ghedina clocked a course record time for the Lauberhorn course in training on Thursday for Saturday's Alpine World Cup men's downhill.
Ghedina, the winner of last weekend's downhill in Chamonix, France, roared down 4,260-metre course, the longest on the World Cup circuit, in two minutes, 24.58 seconds.
His time eclipsed the record of 2:25.09 set by Austrian Werner Franz on Wednesday. The previous record had been set by Marc Girardelli of Luxembourg in 1989.

Ghedina, who is locked in a battle with Luc Alphand of France for the lead in the downhill standings, won the first of back-to-back downhills the last time races were staged on the Lauberhorn in 1995.
Adrien Duvillard of France had the day's second best time of 2:24.85 followed by Norway's Atle Skaardal in 2:24.98.
Franz, second in Wengen in 1995, could not match his preformance from first day training and slipped to fourth best with a clocking of 2:25.18.
Alphand, the reigning downhill champion and the winner of two races already this season, was sixth quickest in 2:25.49.
